original_value: Automatic extraction of buildings in urban and residential scenes has become a subject of growing interest in the domain of photogrammetry and remote sensing, particularly since the mid-1990s. Active contour model, colloquially known as snake model, has been studied to extract buildings from aerial and satellite imagery. However, this task is still very challenging due to the complexity of building size, shape, and its surrounding environment. This complexity leads to a major obstacle for carrying out a reliable large-scale building extraction, since the involved prior information and assumptions on building such as shape, size, and color cannot be generalized over large areas. This paper presents an efficient snake model to overcome such a challenge, called Super-Resolution-based Snake Model (SRSM). The SRSM operates on high-resolution Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR)-based elevation images—called z-images—generated by a super-resolution process applied to LiDAR data. The involved balloon force model is also improved to shrink or inflate adaptively, instead of inflating continuously. This method is applicable for a large scale such as city scale and even larger, while having a high level of automation and not requiring any prior knowledge nor training data from the urban scenes (hence unsupervised). It achieves high overall accuracy when tested on various datasets. For instance, the proposed SRSM yields an average area-based Quality of 86.57% and object-based Quality of 81.60% on the ISPRS Vaihingen benchmark datasets. Compared to other methods using this benchmark dataset, this level of accuracy is highly desirable even for a supervised method. Similarly desirable outcomes are obtained when carrying out the proposed SRSM on the whole City of Quebec (total area of 656 km2), yielding an area-based Quality of 62.37% and an object-based Quality of 63.21%.

result.paraphrase: Automatic building extraction from urban and residential scenes has attracted increasing attention in photogrammetry and remote sensing since the mid-1990s. The active contour, or snake, model has been explored for extracting buildings from aerial and satellite images. Yet the task remains highly difficult because building size, shape, and the surrounding environment are complex. This complexity is a major barrier to dependable large-scale building extraction, since prior knowledge and assumptions about buildings—such as shape, size, and color—do not generalize well over large areas. To address this challenge, the paper introduces an efficient snake model called the Super-Resolution-based Snake Model (SRSM). SRSM works on high-resolution elevation images derived from LiDAR, called z-images, which are produced by applying a super-resolution process to LiDAR data. Its balloon force model is also enhanced so that it can shrink or inflate adaptively rather than inflating continuously. The method is suitable for city scale and beyond, with a high degree of automation and no need for prior knowledge or training data from urban scenes, making it unsupervised. It achieves strong overall accuracy across multiple datasets. On the ISPRS Vaihingen benchmark datasets, the proposed SRSM attains an average area-based Quality of 86.57% and an object-based Quality of 81.60%. Relative to other methods on this benchmark, this accuracy is highly desirable even for a supervised approach. Likewise, applying the proposed SRSM to the entire City of Quebec, with a total area of 656 km2, produces an area-based Quality of 62.37% and an object-based Quality of 63.21%.
